analysis.title: Bounce Or Bull? Goldman's Trading Floor Can't Agree, So Clients Are Selling Vol, Collaring Stocks And Levering Up In Small Caps
key_insights: Goldman's TMT trader Peter Callahan says there is relatively little consensus in the market. Clients are split on whether the rally is a bear-market bounce or the start of a new bull leg.
Week of Nov 9-13: S&P 500 +2.5%, VIX down about a quarter, yields up, dollar up, gold -4.6%, bitcoin down almost 10%.
Goldman's shares desk describes the week as a rotation. Nvidia lost about $500B of market cap while AMD and Broadcom together added more than $500B. Net change in AI market value was roughly zero.

Long-only funds were the sellers of NVDA and recycled cash into hyperscalers and other large-cap tech. Retail posted the biggest opening bid ever recorded in NVDA after the founder's exit. Both long-onlies and hedge funds were moderate net sellers on the week.
Macro has gotten tougher per the cash desk: VIX at 20, 10-year back at 5.13% after hot CPI, dollar breaking out, oil back in the high-$90s.

Next week's calendar: Nvidia earnings Tuesday after the close (first under interim CEO Colette Kress), US retail sales, FOMC minutes Wednesday, Walmart and Alibaba Thursday. Options price a 1.93% S&P move through Friday.
Derivatives desk: positioning is light (US net leverage at five-year lows) and the Panic Index is 6.5 out of 10. The S&P rallied without call skew rising, so clients did not chase upside calls.
Clients are using costless collars. With index skew bid, a 3-month SPX put 10% out of the money is fully funded by a call only 5.5% out of the money, versus 6.7% this summer.

VIX puts have traded more volume over the last 10 sessions than at any other point in 2026. The desk says clients have more confidence in lower vol than in higher spot after last Thursday's extreme moves.
The article argues the short-vol trade is crowded and the entry point is poor. VIX closed at 19.3 and Nomura's McElligott sees a new floor near 18, so there is only about 1.3 vol points of room.
One-week average-stock realized vol hit the mid-60s, exceeded only by Covid and Liberation Day in the eight-year chart. S&P 1-month realized vol is about 22 against 1-month implied of about 14.

Futures desk: Russell 2000 futures funding richened 13bps on Nov 11, against a median daily change of 6bps. This points to leveraged long demand, probably from Other and Non-Reportable CFTC cohorts and not large institutions. The Russell fell 1.7% the next day.

Asset manager gross longs in Russell futures were positively correlated with SOFR earlier in 2026. They liquidated small caps when more or higher-for-longer rate hikes were priced, and the market has just priced more hikes.

Fed funds futures added about 40bps of hikes between now and Q3 next year after hot CPI and Governor Waller's suggestion that a 50bp hike be on the table in December. 2-year yields rose 42bps from last Friday's lows and 30-year yields rose 25bps, with breakevens stable, so the move was mostly real yields. Goldman's economists added a third hike to their forecast.

The rates selloff flipped short-term trend signals negative across the curve. Goldman strats expect modest selling next week, and the thresholds for significant medium and long-term trend buying are further out of reach.

Oil positioning: managed money net length in Brent and WTI fell $8B in the week through Nov 3, then open interest fell another $9.3B through Nov 10. Brent was down 20% month-to-date near $90, then rebounded 4.7% as peace talks stalled. Open interest rebuilt $3B on Thursday, Friday flows showed fresh length and rising demand for upside options, and Energy was the most net bought sector in the prime book.

Sector desks: Nasdaq 100 up about 370bps with semis up about 840bps. Software dispersion has risen, Internet is hard to trade, and large biopharma (LLY +6%) leads the broadening trade while clients worry about valuations.
Financials lagged the S&P by about 200bps, with the heaviest US financials selling in the prime book in eight months and the most negativity in Consumer Finance on regulatory fears.
Industrials rose 350bps led by small and mid-cap AI names (Modine +43%, AAON +40%, CECO +26%), while Corteva fell 22% on a weak Q4 outlook and homebuilders fell as rates rose.

Energy specialists report flight-to-safety demand concentrated in natural gas E&Ps and midstream, with a preference for Gas E&Ps such as EQT and AR where specialist positioning has been negative most of the year.

The author's read is that the market is exhausted and underinvested and is relying on the calendar. A bear-market bounce is judged the more likely answer. Goldman's macro desk and Morgan Stanley's trading platform instead see a squeeze into year-end, and BTIG's Krinsky called the Nvidia bounce a gift to sell.

The Goldman energy specialist notes a preference to hide in Gas E&Ps, where specialist positioning has been more negative most of the year.
Same Gas E&P preference as EQT. Investor inbounds centered on the natural gas complex.

sector_views.rationale: Large biopharma is the winner of the broadening trade, but clients report vertigo about valuations, including PFE vs NVDA P/E comparisons.
Clients want safety and are hiding in natural gas E&Ps and midstream given the uncertain oil macro, falling risk premium and midterm election risk to power.
The sector lagged the S&P by about 200bps, the prime book saw the heaviest selling in eight months, and Consumer Finance faces regulatory fears.
Up 350bps on the week led by small and mid-cap AI names, while homebuilders sank on higher rates.
Callahan describes a blank slate on positioning and sentiment. Semis rebounded about 840bps and then caught down to NVDA on Friday. Software dispersion is higher.

earnings_insights: Nvidia reports Q3 results Tuesday Nov 17 after the close, its first call under interim CEO Colette Kress. No consensus figures are given.
Also reporting next week: Home Depot (Tue), Target, TJX and Lowe's (Wed), Walmart, Alibaba, Ross and Gap (Thu), plus Palo Alto and China internet names.

Reported this week: Ionis fell 21% on a data miss and lowered guide. Legend fell 24% after warning on Q4 and 2027 estimates. Heartflow fell 18% on a beat and raise. Corteva fell 22% on a weak Q4 outlook.
Goldman's health care specialist says large biopharma has benefited from a strong 3Q earnings cycle.

A Goldman scatter of S&P 1-month realized vs implied vol shows no other dot as far to the right as the current reading.
A chart of one-week average-stock realized vol shows the mid-60s reading exceeded only by Covid and Liberation Day in an eight-year history.
A chart of the implied fed funds path compares a week ago (orange) with now (blue).
vol_and_positioning: US net leverage is at five-year lows. The Goldman Panic Index is at 6.5 out of 10, down from the levels last weekend that evoked Covid, the GFC and Liberation Day.
Thursday Nov 5 was the biggest put volume session in history.
5-day S&P call skew stayed near its lows while spot rose sharply, so there was no chase in upside calls.
Index skew is bid (25d put/25d call ratio), allowing costless collars. The 3-month SPX 10% OTM put (S&P near 6,805) is funded by a call about 5.5% OTM (near 7,980) through mid-February.
VIX put volume over the last 10 sessions is the highest of any stretch in 2026.
One-week average-stock realized vol reached the mid-60s, exceeded only by Covid and Liberation Day. S&P 1-month realized vol is about 22 against implied of about 14.
Russell 2000 futures funding richened 13bps on Nov 11, which suggests demand for leveraged longs from retail-type cohorts. Asset manager Russell futures longs track SOFR pricing negatively.
Goldman strats expect only modest CTA selling next week, and the medium and long-term trend thresholds for buying are further out of reach.
Prime book: Energy was the most net bought sector globally and US financials saw the heaviest selling in eight months. Long-onlies and hedge funds were both moderate net sellers.
geopolitical: Peace talks stalled and escalation fears returned, lifting Brent 4.7% ahead of the weekend.
Trump trip to China is on Wednesday's calendar.
Midterm election risk is cited as a driver of uncertainty in the power complex and as the factor that cut oil's war premium.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's macro desk goes further than Callahan and sees a squeeze into year-end, similar to Nick Savone and the entire Morgan Stanley trading platform.

BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky called the Nvidia bounce a gift to sell as the dollar breaks out.

tension_points.bull_case: Callahan and Goldman's macro desk see cleaner positioning, a blank slate on consensus and a possible squeeze into year-end. Morgan Stanley's trading platform is described as similar, and December seasonality usually helps.
tension_points.bear_case: Long-onlies are selling NVDA and hedge funds are adding shorts. Nobody is buying calls, and the only leveraged buying is in small caps by small players. A 50bp hike is possible on Dec 9. The author judges a bear-market bounce the more likely answer, and BTIG's Krinsky called the Nvidia bounce a gift to sell.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nvidia's Q3 report Tuesday after the close, the first without Jensen Huang, and the Dec 9 FOMC decision. The author says the bounce tends to end the moment someone delivers actual news.

tension_points.bull_case: Clients see lower vol as the lowest-conviction way to be bullish, since VIX fell and the options market already charges for a calmer world. VIX puts have traded record 2026 volume.
tension_points.bear_case: VIX at 19.3 is barely above the new floor of about 18, so there are only about 1.3 vol points of room. Realized vol of about 22 runs well above implied of about 14, and Nvidia earnings and a possible 50bp hike come within weeks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A VIX close below the roughly 18 floor Nomura's McElligott cites would support the bull case. A realized-vol spike around the Nvidia print or the Dec 9 FOMC would break it.

tension_points.bull_case: Retail Favorites jumped 5% and Russell 2000 funding richened 13bps on Nov 11, which suggests leveraged demand for small caps.
tension_points.bear_case: Fed funds futures added 40bps of hikes, 2-year yields rose 42bps, and asset managers have historically sold Russell futures when SOFR pricing rises. The Russell fell 1.7% the day after the funding jump.

theme_stances.key_argument: The floor describes long-only selling, hedge fund shorting, no call buying and a crowded vol-short trade, which the author reads as an exhausted market hoping the calendar does the work.
theme_stances.evidence: there appears to be relatively LITTLE CONSENSUS in the market right now

theme_stances.key_argument: Put volume is chasing only about 1.3 vol points between the 19.3 close and the roughly 18 floor, while realized vol sits well above implied.
theme_stances.evidence: VIX puts have traded more volume in the last 10 sessions

theme_stances.theme: small cap leverage vs hiking Fed
theme_stances.key_argument: Rate-sensitive small caps drew leveraged retail buying into a front-end rate shock, while institutions have sold Russell futures when more hikes are priced.
theme_stances.evidence: an extended rate hiking cycle still presents an imminent threat
